title: Applied science: identification, prediction and decisions
summary: Connected worked tutorials in causal inference, forecasting, survival, ranking, optimization, synthesis, spatial analysis and survey/high-dimensional reasoning.

lessons.title: From a scientific question to a transported estimand
lessons.outcome: Standardize stratum effects to a declared target population and show how a crude comparison can reverse the sign of a positive effect.
lessons.lab: Transport the same stratum-specific effects from the trial mix to the target population, then compare both with the crude treated-minus-control difference.
lessons.verification: Trial ATE 1.8 and transported target ATE 1.2 come from the same stratum effects; the crude difference is -1.3, with the opposite sign.

lessons.title: Overlap, weighting and the population a result describes
lessons.outcome: Show that inverse-probability weights balance a finite population exactly, that overlap weighting changes the target population and that concentrated weights shrink the effective sample size.
lessons.lab: Recover the treatment effect by inverse-probability weighting in an exact population table, then compare the overlap-weighted effect with the population effect.
lessons.verification: The weighted effect is exactly 2; overlap weighting gives 2.8 against the population effect 3.4; effective sample sizes are 3 for equal weights and 2809/2503 for weights 1, 1, 1 and 50.

lessons.title: Sensitivity analysis and negative-control reasoning
lessons.outcome: Locate the tipping point at which an unmeasured confounder would explain an observed effect and use a negative control to expose bias that a sensitivity grid does not reveal.
lessons.lab: Tabulate bias-adjusted effects over confounder prevalence and strength, then compare treated and untreated means of a negative-control outcome.
lessons.verification: The observed effect 3 falls to 0 at prevalence 0.5 with strength 6 and turns negative beyond it; the negative-control difference is 1.33 despite a known zero effect; reliability 0.5 attenuates a slope of 2 to 1.

lessons.title: Staggered adoption and uncontaminated group-time contrasts
lessons.outcome: Estimate group-time effects under staggered adoption with uncontaminated comparison groups and show how an already-treated control erases a real effect.
lessons.lab: Recover cohort-specific dynamic effects at period 4, then repeat the contrast using the already-treated early cohort as the control.
lessons.verification: At period 4 the early cohort's effect is 6 and the late cohort's is 2, while the contrast against the already-treated cohort is 0.

lessons.title: Longitudinal interventions and the sequential g-formula
lessons.outcome: Evaluate static and dynamic treatment regimes with the sequential g-formula and show how freezing a mediator distribution removes part of the total effect.
lessons.lab: Enumerate never-treat, always-treat and dynamic regimes over the intermediate covariate, then hold the mediator at its untreated distribution.
lessons.verification: Never treat 2.2, the dynamic policy 4.75 and always treat 7.6 lie in that order; freezing the mediator distribution loses 0.4 of the total effect.

lessons.title: Target-trial alignment and sequential treatment weights
lessons.outcome: Align a target-trial time zero, verify a sequential inverse-probability policy value by exact summation and reject covariates that were not available at baseline.
lessons.lab: Compute the always-treat value by sequential weighting over an exact probability table, then check two records for availability after assignment.
lessons.verification: The weighted always-treat value is 7.2 over probabilities summing to 1, and one record whose availability time follows assignment is rejected as a baseline variable.

lessons.title: Forecast vintages, revision histories and overlapping origins
lessons.outcome: Reconstruct as-of vintages from revision histories, forecast only from information available at each origin and show how a revised backtest leaks later information.
lessons.lab: Forecast event four from the vintage available at cutoff four, then repeat the backtest with the later revision of event two.
lessons.verification: The vintage-aware forecast is 18, the backtest that uses the revision of 14 to 50 gives 36, and four overlapping two-step forecasts cover only three unique target events.

lessons.title: Coherent hierarchical forecasts and covariance-weighted reconciliation
lessons.outcome: Reconcile hierarchical forecasts with ordinary and covariance-weighted projections and show that coherent forecasts can still be physically implausible.
lessons.lab: Reconcile an incoherent total with its components by OLS and weighted projections, then inspect a coherent forecast with a negative component.
lessons.verification: OLS reconciliation turns base forecasts 12, 4 and 5 into 11 = 5 + 6; trusting the total moves it back toward 12 (about 12.0 = 5.5 + 6.5); a nonnegative refit gives bottom forecasts 0 and 2.5.

lessons.title: Forecast calibration, quantiles and operational decision loss
lessons.outcome: Choose an order quantity from the newsvendor critical fractile under asymmetric loss and show how pooled interval coverage can hide a failing horizon.
lessons.lab: Compute the critical fractile and cost-minimizing quantity, then split interval coverage by forecast horizon.
lessons.verification: Critical fractile 0.8 selects quantity 3 with expected cost 4.67 against 5.0 for the mean policy; coverage is 1.0 at the first horizon but 0.4 at the second.

lessons.title: Survival risk sets, delayed entry and partial likelihood
lessons.outcome: Compute Cox partial likelihoods by hand from risk sets, including delayed entry, and locate the maximizing coefficient.
lessons.lab: Evaluate the log partial likelihood at coefficient 0 with and without delayed entry, then search a grid for the maximizer.
lessons.verification: The log partial likelihood is -log(12) = -2.485 at coefficient 0 and -log(6) = -1.792 with delayed entry; the grid maximum 0.35 matches the closed form log(2)/2 = 0.347.

lessons.title: Censoring-aware likelihoods, AFT models and time scales
lessons.outcome: Write censored and left-truncated likelihood contributions, fit a Weibull model by maximum likelihood and interpret an AFT time ratio.
lessons.lab: Compare the censored exponential rate with the naive rate, add delayed entry, then fit Weibull models without and with a binary AFT covariate.
lessons.verification: Exponential rates 0.15 (censoring-aware), 0.25 (naive) and 0.214 (delayed entry); the AFT fit returns time ratio 2, hazard ratio about 0.41 and shape about 1.29 with gradient norms below 1e-5.

lessons.title: Competing risks and proportional-hazards diagnostics
lessons.outcome: Accumulate cumulative incidence under competing risks, contrast it with one minus Kaplan-Meier and test proportional hazards with an episode-split time interaction.
lessons.lab: Compute cause-specific cumulative incidence for four complete records, then fit constant and episode-split Cox models to simulated data whose effect reverses after time 1.
lessons.verification: Each cause has incidence 0.5 while one minus Kaplan-Meier gives 0.625; the constant log hazard ratio is 0.54, while the split model gives 0.86 before time 1 and a change of -1.68 (SE 0.30) after it.

lessons.title: Candidate generation, cold start and retrieval ceilings
lessons.outcome: Generate recommendation candidates from item co-occurrence, measure the retrieval ceiling with candidate recall and define an explicit cold-start policy.
lessons.lab: Score unseen items by Jaccard similarity to the target user's history, check recall at 2, then rank items by popularity for a user without history.
lessons.verification: Items i3 and i4 score 1/3 and i5 scores 0, so recall at 2 is 1 for i4 but 0 for i5, which no reranker can recover; the cold-start policy ranks i3 first.

lessons.title: Pairwise learned ranking and defensible negative sampling
lessons.outcome: Train a pairwise BPR ranking objective with an independently checked gradient and keep future positives out of negative sampling.
lessons.lab: Train pairwise logistic ranking weights and compare the analytic gradient with finite differences, then sample negatives that respect attribution and reporting delays.
lessons.verification: Training lowers the pairwise loss from log 2 = 0.693 to 0.081 with all margins positive; the negative sampler returns only c at time 5 and c and d at time 9.

lessons.title: Logged-policy evaluation, support and variance control
lessons.outcome: Estimate a new policy's value from logged data with inverse propensity scoring and a doubly robust correction and show how clipping trades bias for variance.
lessons.lab: Recover the new policy's value by IPS and by doubly robust estimation, then clip the importance weights.
lessons.verification: IPS and doubly robust estimates both equal 0.5 against a logging-policy average of 0.32; clipping lowers the estimate to 0.34.

lessons.title: Optimization duality and the scope of shadow prices
lessons.outcome: Solve a small linear program, verify its dual shadow price and show that the price is valid only within its local sensitivity range.
lessons.lab: Verify the primal allocation and the shadow price of the binding resource, then apply a resource change beyond the local range.
lessons.verification: Allocation (3, 2) has value 13 and shadow price 1, matching a finite-difference derivative; raising the resource from 5 to 9 gives 16, not the 17 the local price predicts.

lessons.title: Integer decisions, relaxation bounds and solver certificates
lessons.outcome: Solve a binary allocation exactly, compare it with its linear-programming relaxation bound and show that rounding the relaxation can violate a resource constraint.
lessons.lab: Solve the binary allocation and check its feasibility and integrality, then round the fractional relaxation.
lessons.verification: The integer optimum is 14 with choice (0, 1, 1), below the relaxation bound 14.8; rounding the relaxation costs 11, exceeding the budget of 9.

lessons.title: Scenario decisions, minimax policies and information value
lessons.outcome: Compare expected-cost and minimax decisions across demand scenarios and compute the expected value of perfect information.
lessons.lab: Choose a quantity by expected cost and by worst-case cost, then compute how much perfect scenario information would save.
lessons.verification: Expected cost selects 4 (expected cost 4.3), minimax selects 10 (worst cost 8) and the expected value of perfect information is 4.3.

lessons.title: Estimated heterogeneity and prediction in research synthesis
lessons.outcome: Estimate between-study heterogeneity with the DerSimonian-Laird method and distinguish a confidence interval for the mean effect from a prediction interval for a new study.
lessons.lab: Compute tau-squared and the random-effects mean, then compare confidence and prediction half-widths.
lessons.verification: tau-squared = (11.1875 - 3)/75 = 0.109 and the mean is 0.475; the prediction half-width 0.750 is about twice the confidence half-width 0.379.

lessons.title: Dependent effects, missing studies and synthesis sensitivity
lessons.outcome: Combine dependent effect sizes through their covariance and make a missing-study scenario explicit in a synthesis sensitivity analysis.
lessons.lab: Compare the variance of the same mean under independent and correlated effects, then add two hypothetical unpublished negative studies.
lessons.verification: The mean stays 0.5 while its variance rises from 0.020 (independent) to 0.035 (dependent); the stated missing-study scenario moves the visible mean 0.5 to 0.24.

lessons.title: Spatial dependence, permutation reference sets and blocked validation
lessons.outcome: Compute Moran's I for clustered and alternating maps, obtain its exact permutation p-value and compare random row splits with spatial blocks.
lessons.lab: Contrast Moran's I for clustered and alternating values on a six-node chain, enumerate all 20 arrangements, then count neighbor edges crossing train and test folds.
lessons.verification: Moran's I is 0.6 clustered and -1 alternating, the exact one-sided p-value is 2/20 = 0.10, and random folds cut 5 neighbor edges against 1 for spatial blocks.

lessons.title: Survey inclusion weights, clustering and population targets
lessons.outcome: Compute Horvitz-Thompson totals with inclusion weights, separate their expectation from one realized sample and derive a cluster design effect.
lessons.lab: Average the Horvitz-Thompson estimator over every possible sample, compare one realized sample, then derive the design effect of cluster sampling.
lessons.verification: The expected Horvitz-Thompson total 16 equals the population total while the realized sample gives 15; the Hajek mean is 4 and the cluster design effect is 2.2.

lessons.title: High-dimensional identification, regularization and validation
lessons.outcome: Show that interpolating a design with more predictors than observations does not establish generalization and that duplicated predictors identify only their sum.
lessons.lab: Fit a minimum-norm interpolating model and a ridge model to 20 observations of 40 predictors, compare errors, then duplicate a predictor.
lessons.verification: The interpolating fit has training error 0 while ridge has test error 1.88 against the true signal; the duplicated design has rank 1, so coefficients (1, 2) and (2, 1) give identical fits.

lessons.title: A scientific decision dossier with explicit rollback conditions
lessons.outcome: Assemble a decision dossier that estimates effects with uncertainty, selects actions on lower bounds under a budget and triggers a declared rollback when evidence is revised.
lessons.lab: Estimate regional effects and standard errors, select regions whose lower bounds justify their cost, then revise the evidence and apply the rollback rule.
lessons.verification: Effects 3, 1 and -1 with standard errors sqrt(1/3), sqrt(4/3) and sqrt(1/12); only north is selected, and after the revision no region qualifies, which triggers the declared rollback.
